intended_object: The continuous map from the underlying space of a ringed space X to Spec R, for R a local ring, that sends every point to the unique closed point (the maximal ideal) of Spec R. This is the underlying map of the morphisms in Vakil's Exercise 7.2.G. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and its use in `ClosedPointHom.hom`.
explanation:
The body is `TopCat.ofHom ⟨fun _ => IsLocalRing.closedPoint R, continuous_const⟩`. This is the constant map, as a morphism in TopCat, from the carrier of X to the carrier of `Spec.sheafedSpaceObj (CommRingCat.of R)`, and its value is Mathlib's `IsLocalRing.closedPoint R`, the maximal ideal as a point of the prime spectrum. That matches the docstring exactly. The local-ring hypothesis is what makes the closed point exist and be unique.

The map is Mathlib's `ContinuousMap.const` applied to a specific point. The definition only adds the TopCat packaging that the base component of a morphism of ringed spaces requires. The source could be any topological space, but taking a ringed space is what its use needs: it is the base of a ringed-space morphism into Spec R. It is a specific map, so it is not too narrow.
